title: Physical backup: base backups, snapshots and the frozen filesystem

videos.script: A dump rebuilds the database from instructions. This lesson copies the files instead. {{files}} The simplest copy is taken with the server stopped. It is perfect, and it costs an outage. {{cold}} The same copy taken while the server runs looks fine, and is not. Each file is copied at a different moment, and a transaction can end up half in the copy. {{torn}} pg_basebackup fixes that by talking to the server. It asks for a checkpoint, copies the files, and collects the log written while it worked. {{basebackup}} A small file called backup_label tells a restored server where to start repairing. {{label}} Then you tamper with one byte of a backup, and watch the manifest catch it. {{verify}} You restore the whole server in seconds, and compare it with the live one. {{restore}} Last, snapshots: the fastest copy there is, and the easiest to take wrongly. {{snapshots}}
